difficulty_reason: The printed proof treats two infinite faces via a finite separator and one infinite face via a uniformly bounded-distance boundary. A path between the two boundary tails gives a bounded-distance pair of opposite indices. Planarity would then force arbitrarily large finite components cut off by balls of a uniform radius, contrary to quasi-transitivity; the remaining fixed-radius separation contradicts one-endedness.
